content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he made “serious mistakes” but would be willing to return to the chipmaker if asked, in his first statement since resigning over news of his extramarital affairs.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he said in a post on X on Tuesday. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Huang added that he regrets his misconduct and is committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said.

Huang resigned last week after news of the affairs, which reportedly involved a fellow co-worker and a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

President Donald Trump on Monday told reporters he thinks Huang “learned a big lesson” and wouldn’t mind seeing him be reinstated. Trump also expressed doubt on whether Alice Huang, the woman he’s reported to have had a relationship with, was actually a spy.

“Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy. I don’t know that she was a spy at all,” he said.
